Trt_Concerns_Desc:
Exclusion of livestock is critical for the recovery of burned vegetation or establishment and protection of new
seedings. The burn area and seed treatment area would be closed to livestock grazing for a minimum period of two growing
seasons to promote recovery of burned vegetation and to facilitate the establishment of seeded species as specified in the 2005
Shoshone and Burley Normal Fire Rehabilitation Plan (#ID-077-2004-008).

Objectives: Closing the burned area and providing rest from grazing is essential for soil stabilization and vegetation recovery. If the fence materials were not available and the entire allotment was closed, there would be a much greater hardship on the permittees that have already been partially displaced by this fire.
Planned_Implementation: Use supervision of the burned areas would be done to insure that they are rested until plant recovery occurs.  The burned allotments would be visited on a regular basis during the grazing season.  Any unauthorized use occurring on the burned area would be properly documented and steps would be taken to insure it does not continue.  \r\n \r\nRecovery of both native and nonnative seeded areas would be monitored for availability to grazing on a yearly basis.  Two technicians will conduct step-point and/or Daubenmire cover surveys and photo plots on fifteen burned grazing units, and in adjacent unburned areas.  Cover within the burned areas will be compared to cover in adjacent unburned areas on the same ecological sites.  The burned and/or seeded areas would be considered recovered and available for grazing when canopy and ground cover in the burned areas measures at least 70% of what is found in the unburned islands and adjacent areas.  The plants must also have well developed root systems extensive enough to prevent being pulled form the soil when grazed, and the grasses need to be producing seed heads.

Objectives: Close area to livestock grazing to promote natural vegetation recovery.
Planned_Implementation:
The fire burned portions of the Browns Gulch and Bruneau Arm allotments. Closing the burned
areas to livestock grazing, beginning immediately, will allow both perennial and annual
vegetation to recover, which will stabilize the area and minimize wind erosion. Closure
objectives/durations within these areas will be identified in the grazing closure decision and/or
agreements to be issued by the Morley Nelson Snake River Birds of Prey National Conservation
Area. No new fence will be constructed for the closures. The entire Browns Gulch allotment will
be closed which will require only that existing fence be repaired. Within the Bruneau Arm
allotment only the burned portion of the allotment will be closed. This will be achieved by using
water to control livestock movement and will not require new fence construction.
Actual_Implementation:
Grazing was closed by agreement for Browns Gulch Allotment.
Grazing resumed in this allotment October 2018.
Grazing was not closed in Bruneau Arm; this pasture was grazed
beginning October 2017.
